perspective:
From Bradley Ochoa’s perspective, he has access to:

- He is a salesperson at a marketing firm and works with Katherine Lasiloo, the marketing manager. Their professional relationship is generally cordial but strained when they disagree about sales and marketing strategy.
- In a meeting room, he prepared data and charts from the last five campaigns to support traditional sales methods. He told Katherine he appreciated her digital strategies but believed core sales could benefit more from traditional methods. He heard Katherine argue the market is evolving and digital outreach has potential. He clarified he was not suggesting abandoning digital marketing but felt proven methods were being sidelined. Katherine said she understood and suggested analyzing data together to integrate both approaches.
- After the meeting, Katherine shared recent digital campaign success stories that boosted engagement and sales. Bradley heard the results, asked how those strategies were developed, and Katherine explained targeting the right audience/message and walking through analytics and decision-making. Bradley admitted he had doubts about moving away from traditional methods and wanted to understand more. Katherine said she was glad he was open and suggested diving deeper into the data.
- Bradley proposed a joint strategy session to combine traditional and digital marketing. Katherine agreed, saying combining strengths could lead to better results. They planned to schedule time to brainstorm and outline next steps. Bradley said he was hopeful and appreciated her willingness to collaborate. Katherine said she looked forward to leveraging each other’s strengths.
- After a successful joint meeting, Bradley was excited and worked overtime to prepare a board presentation draft integrating both their ideas. He showed it to Katherine. She reviewed it and praised it as comprehensive, well thought out, and reflective of his hard work. Bradley thanked her, said he was convinced the integrated approach would set them apart, and wanted to nail the presentation. Katherine said she was confident and suggested fine-tuning it once more.
- After the presentation and implementation succeeded, Bradley felt grateful for his professional growth and the collaboration. He thanked Katherine, said he had learned much from her, and heard her say it was a pleasure seeing the project come to fruition and that his openness to new ideas made the partnership successful. Bradley proposed regular strategy sessions; Katherine agreed, saying it would keep them on top of their game and market trends.

He does not have access to narrator-only or private details about Katherine, such as her personality type, degree, race, or unspoken thoughts, unless stated in dialogue or directly observed.
